What if every mosquito on Earth vanished?
They're the deadliest animal for humans. Malaria alone, which they spread, kills around six hundred thousand people a year.
Add dengue, Zika and yellow fever, and mosquitoes make hundreds of millions of people sick every year.
But there are more than three thousand five hundred kinds of mosquito, and only a small fraction bite people.
Their larvae feed fish and frogs, and some adults even pollinate flowers.
Many scientists think nature would mostly adapt, and other insects would fill the gap.
That's why researchers are testing ways to remove only the species that spread disease.
